data.hypothesis: The measured 128-thread tile was faster than the 192-, 256-, and 512-thread tiles. A 96-thread CTA with a matching 96-source tile uses 2,688 bytes of shared memory and three warps; its smaller footprint may help resource use, while more tile iterations and barriers may offset that benefit. Measure this tradeoff without assuming a speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: The measurements compare tile sizes under the same shared-source-tiling approach, but aggregate timings do not identify per-size effects.
memory_lessons.claim: The 128-thread configuration measured 0.000963178 seconds, compared with 0.000993696 for 192, 0.000996163 for 256, and 0.001087966 for 512; all were correct.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a 96-thread CTA and 96-source tile to test whether its smaller shared-memory footprint offsets additional tile iterations and barriers.

data.notes: The existing kernel derives the tile length and source loading from blockDim.x, so changing the launch values preserves one target per thread, partial-tile handling, output bounds, and the existing barrier pattern. The candidate has no correctness or timing result yet; leave validation and measurement to the official protocol.
transformations: Set block and items_per_block to 96 and shared_memory_bytes to 2,688, matching one 28-byte Particle per staged source and one target per thread.
Keep the kernel implementation unchanged so the experiment isolates CTA/tile granularity; the existing blockDim-based loop stages partial tiles and preserves output guards and barriers.
